utterances.text: We'll tender that under seal, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P00268 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In order to protect your identity, as of now we'll refer to you as K83. Can you tell us briefly about your background. After you completed primary and secondary school, did you do your military service, as was customary in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I served in the army in 1992, finishing in 1993, in September. After my military service, (redacted) (redacted) When I started working, a police patrol came and served me with a summons for an interview at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you eventually join the police force in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked me -- because they had taken my file from the military department, they asked me if I wanted to serve on the reserve force of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About when was it, or when was it, if you can recall precisely, you joined the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When did you join the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, because we have voice distortion, it will be necessary for you to switch off your microphone the moment you've finished your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll try to remember at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. You were about to tell us when it was that you joined the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After you joined, where were you posted?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Suva Reka where we first provided security to the police station, and later on we also went on field missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These field missions were in the municipality of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you posted there in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could focus on 1998 and 1999, or 1999. At that time, were you issued with uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received a uniform, an automatic rifle, a pistol, and a truncheon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999, were you attached to any particular unit or police station?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not attached to a particular unit. We were there just to assist active-duty policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What police station, if any, were you attached to in 1999?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I did not quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where was the police station that you were attached to in 1999 located?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Suva Reka, and there was a police station in Suva Reka where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your leave, just so we could get oriented where we're talking about, could I show the witness the document which has now become D00003. Perhaps you could zoom in a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Towards the south centre of the province of Kosovo depicted on this map, do you see the municipality of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And almost in the centre of it is Suva Reka -- Suva Reka town, which is the capital.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And to the west, there is Orahovac municipality, and to the south, you see Prizren municipality.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one last thing I'd like you to point out on this map. You see a red line -- you see red lines on the map, but if you could look at the red line that goes between Suva Reka and Prizren, does that depict the main road between Suva Reka and Prizren?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps we could now look at another map, and this is the document 00615, which is an atlas. A series of maps is inside that atlas, and I'd like to look at page 23 of that document. This is a map showing Suva Reka and its environs. Could we focus or zoom in a little bit more on Suva Reka, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You will see the surrounding towns of Suva Reka. There's one I'd like you to focus on in particular. Do you see to the left or to the west of Suva Reka a town called Rastane?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how far is that town from Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I could return to something on the other map, the distance between Suva Reka and Pristina by the road is about how far? Sorry, I see I said Suva Reka and Pristina. Suva Reka and Prizren, about how far is that distance?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eighteen to 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move back to what you were doing in 1998, 1999, in that period did you work full time or part time in the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I worked off and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how long would you be off and how long on?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be off for a month or two, and then I would be on for three, four, five, up to six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the period 1998 to, say, March, 23rd of March, to be precise, 1999, was there a KLA presence in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And kindly tell us what sort of activities the KLA was engaged in in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had some check-points of their own in Rastane facing Drinjevci, Dulje, and they stopped buses and kidnapped Serbs off the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did the police take any action in respect to what the KLA were doing?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the police took steps, but in the time it took the police to get there, they would have already escaped and hidden. They would not be staying around, waiting for police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the municipality, were there on occasion battles between the police and KLA units?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were there battles with KLA units within the town of Suva Reka itself, in the heart of the town of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some battles on the road towards Rastane.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How far were they from the town itself, the town centre?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 2, 2 and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were there any actual battles within the town of Suva Reka itself between KLA units and the police?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was one assault on a member of the State Security Service, the DB, when the terrorists shot at the man as he was buying newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About when was this?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Apart from that, were there any other battles? I'm speaking of battles with the KLA in Suva Reka itself, the town of Suva Reka itself.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, it was up the road to Rastane, in that area, that day when this incident happened, when they shot at this man from the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I ask you, if you recall, who were the main commanders of the police station in Suva Reka town?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief was Vitosevic, the Commander was Radojko Repanovic, the Deputy Commander was Dragan Borisavljevic, and the Assistant Commander was Nenad Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. When you say Vitosevic was the chief of the police station, yet Repanovic was the commander, what do you mean? What sort of responsibilities did you understand Vitosevic to have as distinct from Repanovic, whom you described as a commander?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand these things, Vitosevic was more in charge of the civilian personnel who worked with passports, ID cards, whereas Commander Repanovic was in charge of the police proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say "police proper," you mean police who did what type of work?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean uniformed police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take you to the 26th of March, 1999. This was a couple days after the NATO intervention commenced. Were you on patrol on the morning of that day?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who, if anybody, were you on patrol with?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, we were four or five on patrol. We set out towards Dzinovce because there were police officers there on a field mission. We went there to take food to them, water, and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you return to Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After that, we returned and stopped outside the SUP building in Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About what time you stopped outside the police building in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time. It was a long time ago. I can't remember the hour --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but -- no, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I know you will not be able to tell us precisely what time, but can you just approximate, between what time and what time?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for an hour or so, not longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. What I was trying to get at, can you just tell us approximately? And please understand, we know after so long you can't really be precise, but just between what time and what time was it that you and your patrol stopped outside the police building in Suva Reka on the 26th of March?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 11.00 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the day?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let me get back to something I asked before. Who were the other members of your parade -- your patrol? Could you name them?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Tanovic, Sladjan Cukaric, Miki Petkovic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who was the person who was in charge of the patrol?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Tanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was Cukaric's role in the patrol? In other words, did he have any command responsibility in the patrol?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but the two of them were superiors to me and Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Were all of you reservists, or only some of you reservists and some full, regular police officers?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanovic, Radovan Tanovic, and Sladjan Cukaric were actual duty policemen, whereas Miki Petkovic and I were reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you said that you stopped outside the SUP building. Do you know if it was a SUP building or an OUP building or just a police station?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the station of the interior, of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, when you stopped outside that police station that day, did you see any vehicles in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Two lorries arrived in camouflage colour, and we stood there watching. Out of the two lorries police officers came out, some police officers who, as far as I remember, had arrived to Suva Reka as assistance, and they set out towards the houses opposite the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. So that we can follow you now, I'd like to place before you an aerial photograph of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we bring up 02349, page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before we look at this photograph, could our learned friend Mr. Stamp tell us who made this photograph, and when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you help, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not at this moment. I could provide the information to my friend in the break. I believe the photograph was made by international agencies who entered Suva Reka and entered Kosovo after the end of hostilities. But I think the real question here at this moment is whether or not the witness can speak to the contents of the document or the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The real question is whether this is a depiction of Suva Reka as it was at the time or at some other time, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm happy with Mr. Stamp's answer. We can continue, and then perhaps the witness, too, will give us an explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Djurdjic. Carry on, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the photograph before you, could you tell us, point out to us where the police station is located on this photograph? I think you'll have to mark it, if I may ask that that be done. One moment. One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I'll ask him to mark the place where the trucks were first with the letter A. I do that because I just want to remain consistent with the way the markings were done in another case. So I want the letters to be consistent. It's just for ease of reference in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The trucks that you saw the policemen coming from, could you just put a letter A as to where these trucks stopped?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document in its unmarked form will be received first, Mr. Stamp, and then in marked form. So we will receive this now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document number, Your Honours, with ID 02349 will be given P00269.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please mark where the trucks were located with an A.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you put a cross or an X at the point where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the police arrived in the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before that, may I just indicate that what the witness has put here looks more like a C with a cross in the middle of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Stamp. We see the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were the police arriving in the trucks led by any person in particular?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We called him --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what they called the commander of the unit of the -- which arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: K83, can you repeat the name -- can you repeat what you called the commander of the unit, please?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cegar "jed".

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did he arrive there?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was standing facing the police station. He was standing next to a jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did he arrive in that jeep?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you put a letter B where he was.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you put a letter C where the police station was.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's the police building that you've put the C there.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The lorries that the police came -- arrived in, how would you describe them? Were they ordinary lorries, or were they armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were military trucks that had some additional work done on them, such as armour on the sides, and they had no tarpaulin on top. They were camouflage military trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like you to just put an arrow in the vicinity of the letter A, pointing to where the police that alighted the trucks went to, or pointing to the direction of where the police that alighted the trucks went to.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did Cegar, the leader of the police who alighted the truck, say anything?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we were standing outside the police station, he came up to the Assistant Commander Nenad Jovanovic, and Assistant Commander Nenad Jovanovic wanted to salute back, according to regulation, as a superior commander should be saluted; however, Cegar 1 started yelling at him and said, What are you staring at? What are you waiting for? Go after these men, who came to assist. And Assistant Commander Nenad Jovanovic then just told us to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the translation I just heard, you referred to the commander of these police units as Cegar 1. Earlier you had said "Cegar 'jed'." You referred to him as Cegar 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Cegar "jed".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter heard "Cegar jedan," "jedan" meaning one. Perhaps the witness can clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You're saying in Serbian that the commander was called Cegar 1?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was his password at the police, his code-name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say his password and his code-name, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's his secret identity code.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Would it be used -- would it be used if you were calling him on the radio?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's get back to the events. Assistant Commander Jovanovic told you to move. Where did your patrol move to?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We moved towards Rastane, straight to the house which had earlier been the base for OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like you to mark on the map where your unit went to after Cegar 1 shouted orders to Jovanovic. Just mark it with a D, where your unit went to.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which building is that?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the OSCE building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you see a building on the map below that building?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you go anywhere in respect to that building?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since some policemen were already in the OSCE building, Cukaric and Tanovic ordered me and Petkovic to go behind the house to provide them with cover in case anyone would shoot at them because there was shooting from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So where did you and Petkovic go to? Could you mark the place where you and Petkovic went to with the letter E.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was here, and Petkovic was here, on the other side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness marked -- well, now he has marked a letter E, indicating where he was, and an L, indicating where the other police officer was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said there was shooting. Do you know who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those policemen who had arrived to help were shooting at those houses. There was shooting from all sides. Everything was happening so quickly, like in a movie.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So could you tell us what happened after you arrived to the vicinity, after you arrived to the vicinity of that building behind the OSCE house?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived at that house, there were four men behind the OSCE building, that house, and Cukaric and Tanovic checked their IDs, whereas the other two of us were on the left and on the right of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After Cukaric and Tanovic checked their IDs, what happened?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A woman, some children, and some elderly people came out of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which house?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That house where Petkovic and I were standing on the sides, the one marked with E and L.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did these women, children, and elderly go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since there was shooting all around, they huddled and ran together in a tight cluster towards the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, there were 30 or 35 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When they ran in the direction of the shopping centre, what happened after? Did Cukaric or Tanovic do or say anything?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they told us to follow them, to see where these people would go. But as we had already set out to follow these people, Cukaric and Tanovic lined the four men against the wall of the house. We continued to follow the people to the pizzeria where some people were temporarily accommodated, and on the way two elderly people were injured, hit in the legs. We returned and told Cukaric and Tanovic that those people who had been in the OSCE house were now all in the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let's get a clarification, just to be sure. The women and children ran from which house, the OSCE house that you marked with a D or the house that you were posted at that you marked with an E?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were only four people in the OSCE house, and they stayed there, whereas from the house we were in they rushed out and went to the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I take it that the women and children rushed out of the house marked E?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What happened to the four men that were lined up by Cukaric and Tanovic?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were killed behind the house, behind the OSCE house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just tell us what you saw happen to them.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were facing the wall, their faces against the wall. They were lined up, and then suddenly there was a burst of gun-fire, and they were killed, all four of them, there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who fired?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanovic and Cukaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These four men, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you and Petkovic went after the women and children who had gone in the direction of the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you saw some elderly people who had been injured. Could you mark with a letter F where you saw the elderly people.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you've marked the F -- the F you marked is on a building. Were they in -- on the building or on the ground in the vicinity of the building?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were on the ground. There's a passageway there, a tunnel, and they were on the pavement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were they a man and a woman, or two women, or two men?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man and a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And where had they been hit?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From your experience and what you saw, what had they been hit with?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from an automatic rifle, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Will you mark the spot where they were? Is that the area of the shopping centre as well?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that the persons -- maybe I should withdraw that and ask a different question. Could you, with a G, put the area of the pizzeria where the women, children, and elderly ran to, put where it was.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did you see them inside the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was the door to the pizzeria locked or open?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Probably someone had the key, one of them had the key, since the pizzeria was closed on that day. But someone must have had a key, and as they went inside, they locked themselves in from the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How did you become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the pizzeria, and when I got there, I saw that they were there and that the door was locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said you returned with the other police officer to where Cukaric and Tanovic were. What happened when you rejoined Cukaric and Tanovic?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was quite frightened. I found it difficult to calm down because everything was happening very quickly and I wasn't feeling well. But nearby there was a cafe of some sort, and Cukaric told me to go and take some alcohol or something, to have a drink and sort of relax and come to, to relax and feel better.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Before Cukaric told you to get the drinks, did he discuss what he was intending to do after that?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't say anything. As I was going to the cafe to take a drink, I passed by the old man and the old woman, and they were still alive at that point. When I came back, they were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know how they died?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see it. I didn't see anything, but I just heard a shot or shots, and when I came back I saw that Cukaric had a rifle in his hands, and then we sat down to have a drink, the drink that I had fetched. This was between the pizzeria and that other building where the people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you came back after you heard the shot, the burst of fire, and saw Cukaric with a gun or a rifle in his hand, where was he in relation to the two now-dead old people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned friend Mr. Stamp says that the witness heard a burst of fire. The witness just said he heard shooting. So could he ask his questions properly in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Stamp, it was "shot" or "shots" and you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After you heard these shots, where did you see Cukaric in relation to the two elderly people that were killed?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was moving around down there towards the pizzeria, between -- well, there's a tunnel here. It's not shown very well, but that's where that sort of tunnel is, where we sat down to have that drink and to have a bit of a rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As you arrived back from the cafe with the drinks and you heard the shots, how far was Cukaric from the two old people?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 5 or 6 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know in what parts of their bodies they were shot?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw just a shot to the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After that, you said you went somewhere with him, all four of you now, to have the drinks. Could you mark on the map with a letter H where you stopped to have the drinks.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that is between two buildings, around the corner from the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After you had the drinks, what happened? Just describe to us what happened after you drank the alcohol.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we had the drink, Tanovic broke the window with his rifle butt and threw a hand-grenade inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry, which window are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The window to the pizzeria, where the people were, and those who escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I'd like you to describe in your own words, slowly and carefully, what happened when -- after Tanovic threw the grenade inside the pizzeria where these people were.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I and Petkovic and Cukaric were standing round -- behind the corner, around the corner, because of all the glass, the shattered glass and the explosion and the shrapnel, to avoid being hit and injured, all you could hear were cries and screams and moans and crying, and after several minutes, a couple of minutes later - not even that much, maybe - a second bomb was thrown in, hand-grenade was thrown in. And when things had calmed down a bit, then they started shooting, Cukaric and Tanovic, with a burst of gun-fire, through the shop window, the window to the pizzeria. So they took turns in shooting until all went quiet and none of the cries could be heard anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who threw the second grenade into the pizzeria where the people were?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cukaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After you ceased hearing the cries of these people, what happened? Did Cukaric or Tanovic instruct you to do anything?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Petkovic stayed there, stayed where he was at the corner, and I crossed over to the opposite side, went past the pizzeria, and went up to the main road where there was a kiosk in order to secure a place because of the civilians and the other people, to prevent them from passing by that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there roughly about an hour and a half, perhaps two hours. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. While you were at the kiosk - and I should ask you to mark it an M - you say you were there to prevent people from going to where the shooting occurred. Just put an M where you stood.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The M is placed right next to the main road, I see. Did any vehicle arrive there of any particular significance?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Dr. Boban arrived, Boban Vuksanovic, and Djordjevic, Mirko Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who are these people?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Vuksanovic was a doctor, and he was in the civilian protection during the war as some sort of commander for civilian defence; and Djordjevic, Mirko, he was the TO commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how long after the shooting into the pizzeria and the time you went to stand at the kiosk, on guard, did these two individuals arrive?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it might have been 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When they arrived, what happened? Did they do or say anything?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Boban Vuksanovic examined the bodies to see if they were all dead. After that, a truck arrived from the direction of Prizren in order to load up the bodies from the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did the truck go to?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first truck was loaded up with the bodies, and it went off back to Prizren, or in that direction. Then a second truck arrived, and that second truck also was loaded up, and it drove off in the direction of Prizren too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These two trucks, where did they stop or where did they park in order to be loaded?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Don't mark it. Don't mark it.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- very well here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us first, please. Tell us where they went to and stopped in order to be loaded.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stopped between this kiosk and the pizzeria. There's a small pavement there, and the truck almost drove up to right in front of the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, who loaded the bodies from the pizzeria onto the truck?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- well, they were elderly people in the civilian defence or from the civilian defence, and there were some children, too, who at that time were still not adults. They were still minors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So did they do it willingly or reluctantly? How did they come to do it?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't know what they were supposed to do. They were told to collect up the livestock. So on that day, they didn't know what they were supposed to do, but then they were called by Dr. Boban Vuksanovic to do that. However, they didn't want to do it, and then Cukaric threatened them and said that they were either going to load up the bodies or they'd end up the same way, like the others who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Apart from these people from the civil defence -- or before I move on, these people who loaded the bodies, they arrived with the trucks; is that correct? Do you understand what I'm asking? I'm asking, the people who loaded the bodies, if they arrived on the trucks.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived in another truck that was going around collecting livestock. It was a rather large truck, and they were going around collecting up the cattle, the livestock - sheep, cows, pigs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, do you know somebody by the name of Jashar Berisha?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you see him that day?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That day in the morning, he came to work at the petrol pump.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What work did he do there?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He tanked up the petrol at the petrol pump.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, while you were waiting at the kiosk after the shooting in the pizzeria, did you see him?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was working that day, and then he was detained at the station when the shooting was taking place around those houses, and when those people were killed by the pizzeria, then he was driven in by Todor Jovanovic. Todor Jovanovic brought him in his car. He brought him to the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who is Todor Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the crime technician, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was he a member of the police force in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he worked in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us now what happened to Jashar Berisha when Jovanovic brought him to the vicinity of the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Boban, he called him to come over and see something, I don't know, to see something; however, Jashar didn't want to get close up. However, Cukaric got hold of him by his arm, pushed him away, and shot him in the back once.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before Cukaric shot him, what was he saying? What was Jashar saying when Boban -- when Dr. Vuksanovic spoke to him?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't want to come up close. He said he didn't deserve it. He said, I don't deserve to be there. I can't remember the exact words he said. He struggled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And after Cukaric shot him, what did they do with his body?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was loaded up, too, his body was loaded up in the truck that went to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you remained there after the shooting for perhaps up to two hours. After that, did you go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I think Cukaric drove me to the health centre because I wasn't feeling well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You weren't feeling well in what way? What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shattered. I felt sick, that kind of thing. I wasn't feeling well. I had a difficult time of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To this day, have you recovered from the illness, the feeling of being shattered, having regard to what you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: VETON SURROI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how it is. Well, the film I saw is never interrupted. Everything goes normally during the day, but when I go to sleep I can't -- actually, I can't sleep. I don't sleep well, and I have nightmares, and when I get up in the morning, I feel tired, as if I hadn't slept the whole night. So that's what happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The next day --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm taking a little bit longer than I expected. I don't think I have much longer, but I wish to turn to the events of the next day, and with three minutes left for this day, I wonder if I could do it on the next day of court sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid we can't go past 1.45 because the courtroom has to be prepared for the next trial. I think it might not be practical to move to a new subject matter now, so we could adjourn until Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And may I quickly ask that the marked document be saved before anything happens to the markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it can't be saved. It will have to be exhibited in its present form.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00270, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll have to go in closed session briefly for the witness to leave, but since we have two minutes, I wonder if I could raise two housekeeping matters, which I don't think would be more than a minute each.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. While that's happening, the court staff will close the screens with a view to the witness leaving, and we will then adjourn and resume on Monday at 2.15. Now, you have two matters, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let me mention the least sensitive one first while the witness is present. On the 26th of February, the judgement in a related case is scheduled to be delivered in the afternoon. We're also scheduled in this case to sit on that afternoon. Your Honours, as it turns out, many of the people who would be likely to be in court, in this court, in trial on that afternoon are also persons who are involved in that case, and although most times the delivery of a judgement, there is no need to call upon counsel, but sometimes it is good to have in court persons who know the details about issues of protective measures in particular that might arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I anticipate your request and say that we are having inquiries made to see whether this hearing can be moved to the morning of the 26th of February. If so, that will be done. If not, we will not sit in the afternoon so as not to interfere with the Milutinovic judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am very grateful, Your Honour. Could the witness be discharged for Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We have to adjourn now to continue on Monday. The staff here will give you directions and assistance over the weekend, and we will continue on Monday at 2.15. If you go now with the court officer, and you'll be assisted further with arrangements over the weekend. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
